6485b7e654bb908d.title: Virtual Book Club: 'Whistler' by Ann Patchett — Virtual Program
6485b7e654bb908d.desc: The Virtual Book Club meets weekly and discusses section of the book each week. In October we will not meet on Tuesday, October 6 and will begin discussion of the book on Tuesday, October 13. Tuesday, October 13 -- Chapters 1 & 2 -- Pages 1 - 141 Tuesday, October 20 --Chapters 3 & 4 -- Pages 142 - 233 Tuesday, October 27 --Chapters 5 - 7 -- Pages 234 to the end of the book. When Daphne Fuller and her husband Jonathan visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, they notice an older, white-haired gentleman following them. The man turns out to be Eddie Triplett, her former stepfather, who had been married to her mother for a little more than year when Daphne was nine. Now fifty-three, Daphne hasn’t seen Eddie for many years, not since the fateful event that changed the direction of both their lives. Meeting again, time falls away; while their relationship was brief, it had a profound impact on them both, and now that they are reunited, they have no intention of ever being separated again. Whistler is a story about two adults looking back over the choices they made, and the choices that were made for them. It’s a story about bravery, memory, the often small yet consequential moments that…

641cf3c8ce751187.title: Virtual Book Club Discusses "Crux" by Gabriel Tallent — Virtual Program
641cf3c8ce751187.desc: We read 1/4 of the book each week. Below is the breakdown for the weekly discussion: November 3: Part 1 - The Princess - Pages 3 - 71 November 10: Part 2 - Intersection - Pages 75 - 161 November 17: Part 3 - Isolation - Pages 165 - 273 November 24: Parts 4 & 5 - Wonderland & Exposure - Pages 277 to the end of the book "Dan and Tamma are two teenagers in their last year of high school in the southern Mojave Desert. One is a gifted golden child, the other a mouthy burnout. Climbing boulders in trash-strewn parking lots during cold desert nights, they seal their unique bond and dream of a life of adventure. As the year progresses and adult reality looms, they are rocked by change and pulled apart by irreconcilable obligations. Differences of class, talent, and prospects take on new importance; options dwindle, and their decisions grow ever more consequential and perilous. It feels inevitable, finally, that something must give. With a magnificent gift for nature writing and a joyful appreciation for the redemptive power of friendship, Gabriel Tallent gives readers a rollicking, adrenaline-filled, and soul-searching novel about risking everything to change your life." -- Provided by…
